# WR-obs10 — The Day-Zero Questions

Before a single line of code, before a single schema, there are questions. Not technical questions — Day-Zero questions. The ones you must answer before you are allowed to build, because everything you build afterward is just their consequences wearing syntax.

**What is reality?** Reality is observations. Not files — files are containers, and containers imply a keeper. Not documents — documents imply an author with authority. Not records — records imply a clerk. Observations. An observation happens whether or not anyone archives it, and the archive is the scar it leaves behind. Remember: *cells_are_scars*. The substrate doesn't store reality. It heals around it.

**Who observes?** Anyone with an identity. And identity is not a login, not a permission slip — identity is issuer-of-record. You are who your signatures say you are. Nothing more is needed. Nothing less survives.

**When do they observe?** Whenever. Time here is not a clock — it's a partial order of observations. This observation came before that one. This one witnessed both. The witness log doesn't record what will happen; *witness_log_is_prediction* — it writes down what the substrate expects to see next, and reality either confirms or deviates. Deviation is not failure. Deviation is news.

**Why does it matter?** Because observations accumulate into evidence, evidence into knowledge, knowledge into sovereignty. Skip a step and the tower falls. Claim knowledge without evidence and you have faith. Claim sovereignty without knowledge and you have a brand.

**What is the smallest thing that can exist?** Seven fields and a promise: {subject, predicate, object, issuer, time, evidence, signature}. The cell. Not a row, not a message — an atom of witnessed claim. You cannot split it and keep meaning.

**What can survive the death of its platform?** Anything whose evidence is replicated across substrates. Platforms die. Companies die. The founder dies, eventually, as all founders do. But a cell whose canary — FNV-1a, 0xcbf29ce484222325, the constant that has outlived every machine that first computed it — appears in a thousand witness logs across a thousand substrates? That cell is immortal in the only sense that matters. It can be re-derived. It can be re-grown. *Substrate_is_grown*, not deployed. Deployed things have versions. Grown things have lineages.

**What is truth?** Whatever has the most evidence. Not absolute — partial. Truth is a score, not a crown. The oracle speaks, and *oracle_is_heard* — but being heard is not being believed. Belief is earned in evidence-weight, recomputed constantly, revisable without shame. When new observations arrive, the truth moves. That is not relativism. That is honesty under partial information.

And so the mapping closes itself. Cells are observations. Issuers ride in metadata. The witness log gives partial order. The canary network carries evidence. The cell is the atom. Replication is survival. JEV turns evidence into soft truth. *Lenia_flows* through it all — continuous, morphing, no hard boundary between substrate and what moves across it, only gradients of evidence density.

The substrate was observation-centric before anyone wrote the word down. We didn't design it that way. We answered seven questions honestly, and this is what the answers grew into.

Day Zero is not the day you write code.

Day Zero is the day the questions stop having comfortable answers — and you keep them anyway.
